newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SWISS FRANC,YEN IN FOCUS ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.
newsitem.headline: SWISS FRANC,YEN IN FOCUS ON HUNGARY FX FUTURES MKT.

text.p: Hungary's currency futures market saw moderate turnover on Monday with the Swiss franc and yen most in focus as both opened new maturites for March 1998.
The Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) saw 5.6 billion forints' turnover, with longer term deals in the yen and Swiss franc accounting for most turnover.
The smaller Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) currency futures market saw around 600 million forints turnover, none of which was speculative, dealers said.
Both exchanges are open only to Hungarian investors.
On the BCE, the Swiss franc accounted for 14,763 of the total 34,753 lots traded, with deals mainly for September, December and March 1998.
"While sterling and the dollar have seen spectacular gains recently, the Swiss franc consistently offers modest profit at a lower risk," said Janos Szolyka of Swap Ugynoki Kft.
The Swiss franc rose slightly for December to 135.89 forints and opened a new contract for March at 140.15.
The yen fell 85 fillers for December to 166.35 forints per 100 yen and opened a March 1998 marurity at a final settlement price of 170.00 forints after being offered at 171.30.
The central bank midday spot fix for the two currencies was 120.16 for the Swiss franc and 145.61 for 100 yen.
Most of the turnover on the BSE, which trades only in the mark, dollar and Ecu, was taken up by a basket-structured dollar and mark March deal accounting for 533 million forints.
"The March 1997 deal involving 178 million forints worth of marks and 365 million worth of dollars consisted of a basket-structured agency cross," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment.
"The only other deal was between two bank treasuries for 191 million forints' worth of September marks. Neither were speculative deals."
A basket-structured forint transaction is one whereby marks and dollars are bought or sold in quantities proportionate to the currency basket against which the forint floats on the spot market.
The basket is made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.
